WHO tuberculosis burden estimates by country and year

Source: R/data.R
tb_burden.Rd

Modelled estimates of tuberculosis (TB) incidence, mortality and related indicators for 215 countries and territories, 2000-2023. This is the data behind the tbprogress app and functions; see data-raw/tb_burden.R for the script that prepares it from the raw file.

Usage

tb_burden

Format

A tibble with 5,117 rows (one per country-year) and 18 variables:

country

Country or territory name.

iso3

ISO 3-letter country code. Unique identifier for a country.

iso2

ISO 2-letter country code. Namibia's code is the text "NA", not a missing value.

iso_numeric

ISO numeric country code.

who_region

WHO region (factor with 6 levels: Africa, Americas, Eastern Mediterranean, Europe, South-East Asia, Western Pacific).

year

Year of the estimate (integer, 2000 to 2023).

population

Estimated total population.

incidence_rate

Estimated TB incidence (all forms): new and relapse cases per 100,000 people per year.

incidence_n

Estimated number of incident TB cases (all forms).

mortality_rate

Estimated TB mortality (all forms, including deaths among people living with HIV): deaths per 100,000 people per year.

mortality_n

Estimated number of TB deaths (all forms, including deaths among people living with HIV). The End TB Strategy deaths target is defined on this number, so tb_progress_summary() uses it for the "mortality" indicator.

mortality_rate_hiv_neg

Estimated TB mortality among HIV-negative people, per 100,000 population.

mortality_n_hiv_neg

Estimated number of TB deaths among HIV-negative people.

mortality_rate_hiv_pos

Estimated TB mortality among HIV-positive people, per 100,000 population.

mortality_n_hiv_pos

Estimated number of TB deaths among HIV-positive people.

case_detection_rate

Case detection rate, also called TB treatment coverage: percent of estimated incident cases that were notified.

notification_rate

Case notification rate (new, relapse and unknown-history cases) per 100,000 population.

case_fatality_ratio

Estimated TB case fatality ratio (deaths divided by incident cases).

Source

World Health Organization (WHO), global tuberculosis programme data (https://www.who.int/teams/global-tuberculosis-programme/data), accessed via the TidyTuesday release of 2025-11-11 (https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2025/2025-11-11, curated by Darakhshan Nehal from the 'getTBinR' package by Sam Abbott, https://github.com/seabbs/getTBinR). The same WHO estimates are published on the WHO data portal, for example "Tuberculosis incidence (per 100 000 population)" (https://data.who.int/indicators/i/13B4226/C288D13).

Licence and attribution. WHO publishes its datasets on data.who.int under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0) together with additional WHO terms (https://data.who.int/about/data/terms-and-conditions). This package follows them: WHO is credited as the source (see the citation below); the data are not altered in meaning; this package, its outputs and its analyses are not endorsed by WHO; and the WHO name and emblem are not used as branding. WHO's separate data policy also limits use to public-health, non-commercial purposes, so the data are used here for educational purposes only. The package licence (MIT) covers the code only.

Changes made. Columns were renamed and re-ordered, a subset of variables was kept, and who_region was converted to a factor. No data values were changed. See data-raw/tb_burden.R.

Suggested citation. World Health Organization 2026 data.who.int, Tuberculosis incidence (per 100 000 population) [Indicator]. https://data.who.int/indicators/i/13B4226/C288D13 (Accessed on 31 October 2026, via the TidyTuesday copy described above).

Details

All rates are estimates produced by the World Health Organization (WHO) using notification data, surveys and modelling. The subset used here does not include WHO's uncertainty intervals, so small differences between countries or years should not be over-interpreted. A few countries have missing values (for example, mortality_rate is missing for every year for the Democratic People's Republic of Korea), and a few territories have a rate of exactly zero in some years.
